title: CIA and at least two other US intelligence bodies reportedly hit in breach of an open-source intelligence system, per NYT
date_note: Korrespondent.net's article of 25 November gives no earlier day; it says the breach was discovered "recently" per the New York Times report of 24 November.
summary: Korrespondent.net, citing the New York Times, reports a breach of an open-source intelligence analysis system used by the CIA and at least two other US intelligence bodies, including the NGA and the ODNI. An anonymous source told AP an unclassified CIA system was breached, that no classified information was involved and that the issue has been resolved. Two NYT sources said preliminary indicators may point to China.
plain: Reports citing the New York Times and an anonymous source who spoke to AP say hackers got into an open-source analysis system used by the CIA and other US agencies. No on-record confirmation is reported.
exec: Anonymous sources say no classified material was involved and the issue is resolved; the breach is not confirmed on the record.
geo_basis: US federal intelligence agencies; the article gives no city

validation.note: Korrespondent.net (relaying the NYT) and KSBY (AP, with its own anonymous source) each state the core fact; no on-record CIA confirmation was read.

review.note: stronger than the source: one source says fixed, not sources
